draft.title: Technologies for hearing loss
card: Sound normally travels through the outer and middle ear to the cochlea, an organ in the inner ear. Hair cells in the cochlea turn the vibrations into nerve signals, and the auditory nerve carries them to the brain.
a device worn on or in the ear that makes sounds louder. It still relies on working hair cells in the cochlea to detect the sound.
a device that picks up sound and turns it into electrical signals. Electrodes placed in the cochlea send these signals to the auditory nerve, so it does not need working hair cells.
Cochlear implants were developed in Australia. They suit people whose hearing loss is due to damaged hair cells and who gain little from a hearing aid.
draft.remember: A hearing aid amplifies sound. A cochlear implant replaces the hair cells' job with electrical signals.

a.q: Which statement correctly describes how a cochlear implant works?
opts: It turns sound into signals sent to the auditory nerve
It makes sounds louder so damaged hair cells can detect them
It repairs the hair cells in the cochlea so they work again
It carries sound to the brain through the middle ear bones
a.why: A cochlear implant converts sound to electrical signals and sends them through electrodes to the auditory nerve. Making sound louder is what a hearing aid does, and that only helps if hair cells still work.
a.clue: Think about what the implant does instead of the hair cells.

b.q: Tom has severe hearing loss because the hair cells in his cochleas are damaged. A hearing aid gives him little help. Why might a cochlear implant help him?
opts: It bypasses damaged hair cells and stimulates the nerve
It amplifies sound enough to make the hair cells work again
It replaces the auditory nerve with a device in the cochlea
It sends sound to the brain without turning it into signals
b.why: The implant sends electrical signals straight to the auditory nerve, so it does not depend on working hair cells. A hearing aid only amplifies sound, which is little use when the hair cells cannot detect it. The implant does not replace the nerve.
b.clue: Which device does not need working hair cells?

a.best: It turns sound into signals sent to the auditory nerve

b.best: It bypasses damaged hair cells and stimulates the nerve
